messages.text: The sun streams in the two broad windows in your sitting room. There is a pipe rack to the right of the sofa. Bullet pock marks are the feature of one wall, and charts and diagrams fill another. An acid stained table sits in the corner. To the west there is your door. To the north there is a plain door. You can see an oil lamp, your armchair and watsons armchair. In watsons armchair there is Watson. Watson is carrying the daily chronicle.
I SEE NO ARMCHAIR THAT YOU CAN TAKE
You are carrying an oil lamp and your money.
You give the oil lamp to Watson.
YOU CANNOT TAKE THE OIL LAMP.

You examine watsons armchair.
 You see watsons armchair.
You are in a hall. To the east there is your door. Below there is the stairway.
You are in an entrance hallway. Above there is the stairway. To the south there is the front door.
You are on Baker Street. To the north there is the front door.

You go north.
 You are in an entrance hallway.

You go up.
 You are in a hall.

You go east.

In watsons armchair there is Watson. Watson is carrying the daily chronicle.

You count your money.
 It totals £5 4/-

YOU CANNOT LOOK THROUGH YOUR DOOR.
